Red run: kill -9 of the guard's child -> Z, lost x3, restarting x4, four defunct children, no recovery in 115 s, dispatch unanswered; same on installed 0.1.211 (out-file ...-909). Live machine during this session: 2012 -> 58551 -> 38872 restarts (18595-18797), 58551 is <defunct> under guard 2070 now.

material.description: Defect: in cwd /Users/dylanwong/fluid/hive, codesearch dual (BM25+vector) answers PeerSpeak/apps/admin/... and PeerSpeak/__tests__/... hits (total_candidates 5, docs_hidden 12, hits_are_nearest_neighbours true) while literal/filename modes in the same cwd scan 2191/2265 git-listed files under ./crates ./vendor ./ui. Pre: dispatch cwd is inside a git repo whose root is R; the ranked index store under R/.gm/code-search (or wherever dual mode resolves it) may carry rows walked from a different root. Invariant: every row the ranked retriever serves names a path relative to R that exists under R (or is git-listed under R). Post: dual mode for cwd R serves only R-rooted rows; an index whose recorded root / digest disagrees with R is detected, logged as a note on the response, and rebuilt from R (or refused loudly) instead of served. Witness plan: locate the resolver (code_index.rs, codesearch verb impl), read hive's on-disk index metadata to see which root it recorded, fix the resolver / add a root-identity check in rs-plugkit, rebuild gm.wasm, re-dispatch the same query in hive and read hive-rooted hits. Scope: this defect only; gm-work git verbs for the commit, dywongcloud attribution only.
material.title: codesearch dual mode is rooted at the dispatch cwd's git root; a foreign/mismatched ranked index is detected and rebuilt or refused with a note, never served
material.witness: Root cause: code_index::collect_files_impl (the one enumeration primitive behind the chunk index, the content digest, the symbol index and scan_deps) walked the disk via host_fs_readdir honouring only <root>/.gitignore, so it crossed the boundary of the nested repository hive/PeerSpeak (a gitlink, 5950 files) that git ls-files -- the universe literal/filename modes use via scan_universe -- excludes; byte-sorted, PeerSpeak/ preceded every lowercase hive directory and each 4 s budgeted pass churned inside it (daemon.log `indexing root=. files=6545`, `resume_at=PeerSpeak/...`). Fix (rs-plugkit commit 3f2e34055e on feat/git-amend-reword, author dywongcloud; crates/plugkit-core/src/code_index.rs, codesearch_rank.rs, wasm_dispatch/verbs/search.rs, CHANGELOG.md): collect_files_impl asks scan_universe::list_scan_universe first and takes a git-sourced listing (index_admits + is_gitlink_directory), disk walk only as fallback; FileEnumeration carries source; index_progress_of carries files_enumerated/file_source/removed_files/pass_ms.total; both dual flows carry index_pass; compact_dual adds index_note when a pass pruned foreign rows. Built by the bound dispatch (exec_js 1791924442223-326-2893a80a41282daf: `cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip1 --no-default-features --features slim --lib` exit 0, sha 9959cec820b9f72f3f60840aa8b677b2dc8e8fccfda6446a604f73366454f930), sideloaded to ~/.agentplug/plugins/gm.wasm (marker local-dev-9959cec820b9, release backup gm.wasm.bak-cb848abc7d0e), adopted by the daemon. Witness: before, `codesearch {query:'hive_zkauth::Roster prove verify_membership'}` in /Users/dylanwong/fluid/hive answered five PeerSpeak/apps/admin/... rows (total_candidates 5); after, the same query answers crates/hive-zkauth/src/lib.rs:257 impl Roster, :297 verify_membership, :286 prove_membership (26 candidates, no PeerSpeak), index_pass {file_source: git, files_enumerated: 875}; first pass removed_files=5129 in 366 ms (pass total 5449 ms); symbol sync files_removed=5445; a scratch-repo deletion answered index_note with removed_files 1. hive's tracked tree untouched (.gm/* is gitignored; no .gm/code-search exists)

Postcondition: every write of .status.json carries queue_depth equal to a fresh readdir count of unclaimed settled files under in/<verb>/ (never the project round-robin index), queue_position equal to the number of unclaimed in-files across the daemon's active projects older than this project's oldest unclaimed one, in_flight_count from the in-flight map, claim_pass_ts/claim_pass_age_ms from the last claim pass that visited this project, and busy_until present only while in_flight_count > 0 or unclaimed work exists. Invariant: for an active project (queued or claimed work) the counts are never served from the 120 s scan cache; the old round-robin pair is renamed project_queue_position/project_queue_depth.

material.acceptance_criteria: witness: scratch daemon with gm_pool_size=2, two exec_js sleep 45000 on project A, then a bash on cold project B and a bash on A: both claimed within 2 s (before the fix B's load blocks the pass until a sleep ends)
material.description: Precondition: all gm pool slots are held by running dispatches and a project not yet loaded receives a ticket. Postcondition: load_plugin registers the shared pool and returns at once when any slot is loaded or busy with the current content hash; it fills a slot only through try_lock on an empty slot; the claim pass (thread::scope workers) completes each tick in bounded time. Invariant: no code path reachable from dispatch_project calls SharedPluginPool::acquire().
material.subject: ProjectPlugins::load_plugin for a stateless shared plugin never waits for a pool slot, so a cold project cannot stall the daemon's claim pass while the gm pool is saturated
material.witness: premise re-witnessed and overturned before acting (exec_js 1791925502026-364-b9c0923659b32107 printed 'load_plugin calls acquire(): false'): in main, ProjectPlugins::load_plugin fills the shared gm pool only through try_lock and treats a busy slot as loaded, so no edit was made there. The row's postcondition (the claim pass completes in bounded time while the pool is saturated) is witnessed in the same run output: fixed3-state-flood.log shows 31 state dispatches in flight (every gm slot held, 6 more unclaimed at the state budget) while the never-loaded project proj-b had its bash claimed 63 ms after it was written and answered at 689 ms, and fixed3-exec-flood.log shows the same cold project claimed at 777 ms with every exec slot held by 40 s sleeps; dispatch_project spawns one thread per claimed request and the standalone watcher now runs that same pass

material.acceptance_criteria: witness: gm_pool_size=4 with defaults (1/1/1 reserved): 6 state-lane slow tickets (codesearch dual or instruction with wait) saturating, then a bash and a git_status: both run within 3 s; status/ledger name the band
material.description: Precondition: gm_pool_size S, reservations r_exec + r_read + r_state <= S (defaults max(1,S/4), max(1,S/4), max(1,S/4)). Postcondition: a ticket of band b takes a physical slot when used_b < r_b, or when the free slots exceed the other bands' unused reservations; state/indexing tickets can never hold the slots reserved for exec or read, and an exec/read ticket is admitted within one scheduling turn whenever its reservation has room. Postcondition: the wrapper extends its deadline in bounded steps while that holds, up to timeout_seconds when given or pollTimeoutCeilingMs otherwise; the eventual timed_out reply carries dispatch_state.queue_position (1-based among this project's unclaimed by mtime), queue_depth (unclaimed count), the daemon's queue_depth/claim_pass_age_ms, and accounting_mismatch when the two disagree. Invariant: a claimed ticket (inflight) or a dead daemon never extends the deadline.
material.subject: gm-mcp keeps polling a ticket that is merely queued_not_yet_claimed with a live daemon up to the caller's timeout_seconds (or the ceiling when none given) instead of failing at the 120 s default, and reports the live queue position
material.witness: postcondition witnessed live through gm-mcp src/cli.js against the scratch daemon (exec_js 1791926950326-406-de83d8df9233d7e5 printed wrapper-witness.stdout run 1): with the exec claim budget held by one session (in_flight 32, queue_depth 1), a bash dispatched with no timeout_seconds logged poll-extended-while-queued at 122.7 s with queue_position 2 and queue_depth 3 and cap_ms 600000 instead of failing at 120 s, and its reply carried queued_poll_extensions 1 and the cap reason naming the poll ceiling; a second bash with --timeout 45 stopped at its own cap (51.4 s) with queued_poll_extension_cap_ms 45000. Invariant: run 4 shows a claimed ticket (claimed_still_in_flight) timing out without extension. Code: dispatch.js QUEUED_POLL_EXTENSION_STEP_MS, callerNamedBudget/queuedExtensionCapMs in runDispatch
material.witness_plan: node src/cli.js against the scratch project with GM_TOOLS_DIR/AGENTPLUG_HOME pointing at the scratch home

material.description: Precondition: a timed_out or diagnostic reply is being composed. Postcondition: daemon.busy is true only when the status reports in_flight_count > 0 or unclaimed work; daemon.queue_depth is echoed with queue_depth_source and compared with the spool scan's project_unclaimed_count; disagreement sets accounting_mismatch: true with both numbers; dispatch_state.note names the ticket's lane (exec/read/state) and whether that lane's claim budget is saturated. Invariant: no field in the daemon block is copied from .status.json without naming its meaning.

material.description: Precondition: scratch home with the built runner, plugins copied, scratch project registered only there. Postcondition: a transcript with timestamps shows, for the unmodified build: bash claim latency and the status queue_depth while an in-file waits; for the fixed build: bash claim latency <= 2000 ms with N >= gm_pool_size slow tickets running, queue_depth == unclaimed in-files at every sample, queue_position correct. Invariant: the live runners serving the user's projects are never signalled, restarted or registered against.
